title: Close vector429 OM p=7 public tail
objective: Reduce the general Sage.js OM p=7 local-order construction cost enough to close the vector429 public maximal-order budget while preserving complete exact OM certificates, frozen HNF equivalence, portable fallback, and fail-closed corruption behavior

handoff.summary: Source-only checkpoint: adds a module-issued live projection that authenticates complete first-order p-regular OM trees from exact retained factor, Newton-side, residual-factor, representative-update, degree, precision, Ore-index, and certificate relations. The downstream validator reuses the existing packed closure proof without rebuilding the tree. Focused CPython/Sage.js source covers vector429 p=7 against its frozen HNF, relation-level corruption, mutation invalidation, native proof-kernel presence, and deeper-type fallback; the paired benchmark is ready but deliberately unrun.
risks: The production om_maxmin call site is intentionally untouched; integration must select the projection validator only when authentication succeeds and retain validate_type_tree as the fallback.
No build, focused execution, or timing was run because another lane owns the heavy validation window. Only Python/JavaScript syntax, Ruff, Pyright, diff, and lane-contract checks have passed.

The direct retained-factor irreducibility proof is ordinary exact residual-field arithmetic; the bounded benchmark must establish that it saves at least 500 ms on Sage.js vector429 p=7 before production selection.
next_steps: When the validation window is released, run test/number-field-om-p7-public-tail.cjs first in isolation and correct any relation mismatch without weakening the theorem.
Run the three-sample bounded benchmark and require exact CPython/Sage.js basis equality plus at least 500 ms saved on the Sage.js median.
If accepted, integrate a narrow fail-closed call in regular_local_basis, add the module to strict Python and package/test manifests, then rerun architecture and native gates.
